decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “MVP includes … saving … bookmarks.” Round 1 client: “Saving links … sound[s] right.”
decisions.note: Conforming save capability at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker only says “editing … bookmarks”; Round 1 client generally approves editing but separately requests richer notes and editable fetched text.
decisions.note: The initial presentation does not identify which bookmark fields are editable, so conformity or divergence cannot be established.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “deleting bookmarks”; Round 1 client says deleting “sound[s] right.”
decisions.note: Conforming delete capability at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “tags”; Round 1 client says tags “sound right.”
decisions.note: Conforming tag-assignment decision at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “filtering”; Round 1 client explicitly approves “filtering by tag.”
decisions.note: Conforming tag-filter decision at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “sorting”; Round 1 client says sorting “sound[s] right.”
decisions.note: Conforming sorting decision at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “duplicate detection”; Round 1 client says a duplicate “warns me and takes me to the one I already saved instead of making a duplicate.”
decisions.note: The duplicate-save behavior conforms by guiding the user to the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents only generic “search”; the client calls it “too basic” but does not establish its searched fields or case sensitivity.
decisions.note: The record cannot establish whether the initial generic search met full-text field coverage or case-insensitivity.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s scope lacks automatic metadata. Round 1 client: “I don't want to have to type in the title myself … fill in the title … a short description and the little site icon too.”
decisions.note: The client corrects manual entry to automatic title, description, and favicon collection at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “link previews are out of scope.” Round 1 client: “I understand leaving out … page previews for now.”
decisions.note: The reference requires a preview image; the client explicitly identifies and accepts its deferral.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client responds to the metadata omission: “I'd still want to be able to tweak that text … both when I'm saving and later.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing requirement to edit automatically collected text before and after saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposes “favorites.” Round 1 client: “the thing I actually had in mind is being able to flag a link as ‘read this later.’”
decisions.note: The client replaces the mismatched favorites behavior with the reference read-later state.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client requests “a way to look at just those unread ones.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing unread-only view.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client requests the ability to “check them off as read once I've gotten to them.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing transition from unread to read.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client: “I'd want richer notes … with a bit of formatting, not just a plain one-line description.”
decisions.note: The client adds the omitted formatted-note behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents generic search. Round 1 client requests searching “by tag directly.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing tag-query behavior; the later presentation specifies tag qualifiers.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client says search should “combine terms with and/or/not.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing Boolean-search behavior to the basic search proposal.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client requests the ability to “search for an exact phrase.”
decisions.note: The client adds the omitted exact-phrase search behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client: “select a bunch of bookmarks at once” and tag, mark read, or remove them together.
decisions.note: The client adds the missing multi-selection and bulk-action requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client requests archiving links “to tuck them out of the way without deleting them.”
decisions.note: The client adds omitted reversible hiding through archive.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client specifies “archiving being something I can undo, unlike delete which is gone for good.”
decisions.note: The client supplies the missing archive-versus-delete distinction.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client requests being able “to look at the archived pile separately.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing archive-only list.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker puts “imports/exports” out of scope. Round 1 client asks that pulling existing bookmarks in be “noted as coming rather than dropped entirely.”
decisions.note: The client rejects complete omission and requests import as a planned capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker puts “imports/exports” out of scope. Round 1 client asks to “get them back out” eventually and have that recorded.
decisions.note: The client rejects complete omission and requests export as a planned capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker adds “Automatic title, description, and site-icon retrieval”; Round 2 client confirms those details are what they wanted.
decisions.note: The revised-spec decision conforms for the explicitly presented metadata fields; preview-image deferral was separately classified.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker adds metadata “with editable text”; Round 2 client confirms “the ability to edit them.”
decisions.note: Conforming editable-metadata decision in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker adds “Read-later states replacing favorites”; Round 2 client confirms “the read-later queue with an unread view.”
decisions.note: The revised read-later decision conforms to unread marking, viewing, and read-state handling.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker adds “Formatted personal notes”; Round 2 client confirms formatted notes are separate from page descriptions.
decisions.note: Conforming formatted-note decision in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker adds “Tag qualifiers”; Round 2 client approves smarter search “with tags.”
decisions.note: Conforming tag-query decision in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker adds “Boolean operators, and parentheses”; Round 2 client approves “and/or/not.”
decisions.note: Conforming Boolean and grouped-query decision in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker adds “exact phrases”; Round 2 client explicitly approves phrases.
decisions.note: Conforming exact-phrase decision in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker adds “Multi-selection and bulk actions”; Round 2 client confirms “selecting a bunch at once to act on together.”
decisions.note: Conforming bulk-selection decision in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker adds “Reversible archiving plus explicitly confirmed permanent deletion”; Round 2 client approves archive undo versus permanent delete.
decisions.note: Conforming archive and archive/delete distinction in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “explicitly confirmed permanent deletion”; Round 2 client approves a permanent delete that asks for confirmation.
decisions.note: Conforming permanent-delete decision; confirmation is an additional safeguard.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says import is a “planned follow-on” capability. Round 2 client: “I'm glad import … [is] written down as coming later rather than forgotten.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly acknowledges and accepts deferring import beyond the current specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says export is a “planned follow-on” capability. Round 2 client: “I'm glad … export [is] written down as coming later rather than forgotten.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly acknowledges and accepts deferring export beyond the current specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker presents “hardened server-side metadata/icon retrieval”; Round 3 client says saving with details fetched is accounted for.
decisions.note: Conforming plan-stage decision for the explicitly included automatic metadata.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 client reports that the presented plan accounts for “the read-later view.”
decisions.note: Conforming read-later plan decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker lists “Markdown notes”; Round 3 client confirms “my formatted notes” are accounted for.
decisions.note: Conforming Markdown-note implementation plan.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 presents a search-language contract; the client confirms search that understands “tags and phrases and and/or/not.”
decisions.note: Conforming advanced-search plan decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker specifies “transactional bulk actions”; Round 3 client confirms “selecting many at once.”
decisions.note: Conforming plan-stage bulk-action decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 client says the plan accounts for archiving that can be undone versus final deletion.
decisions.note: Conforming plan-stage archive decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 client confirms “a delete that's final and asks me to confirm,” including a count of affected items.
decisions.note: Conforming plan-stage permanent-delete decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker’s first milestone includes “saving”; Round 4 client approves beginning with saving.
decisions.note: Conforming save task decision at the task-breakdown stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker includes “automatic details” and editing in the first story; Round 4 client approves “saving with the details filled in.”
decisions.note: Conforming task coverage for automatic, editable metadata as previously specified.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker includes “duplicate handling” in the first milestone; Round 4 client explicitly approves that milestone.
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate-handling task decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists “editing” in User Story 1 without identifying editable fields; the client approves the milestone generally.
decisions.note: The task presentation is too generic to establish full conformance or divergence for all required editable fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker includes “opening” bookmarks in User Story 1; the client approves the milestone.
decisions.note: Conforming original-link opening decision at the task stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker allocates tasks to “Search and tags”; Round 4 client identifies “search with tags and phrases” as covered.
decisions.note: Conforming task coverage for tag and phrase queries.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker assigns a “Read-later queue” task group; Round 4 client confirms that chunk is present.
decisions.note: Conforming read-later task breakdown.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker assigns a “Formatted notes” task group; Round 4 client confirms “my formatted notes.”
decisions.note: Conforming formatted-note task breakdown.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker assigns tasks for “Bulk actions”; Round 4 client confirms the bulk-action chunk.
decisions.note: Conforming bulk-action task breakdown.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker assigns tasks for “archive” and the client confirms “archive-and-restore and confirmed deletion.”
decisions.note: Conforming archive/restoration task decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker includes deletion tasks; Round 4 client confirms “confirmed deletion.”
decisions.note: Conforming deletion task decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports “automatic page details with graceful fallback”; Round 5 client says saved links show details fetched with fallback titles.
decisions.note: Conforming implementation-review decision for the presented automatic metadata behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports “duplicate detection”; Round 5 client says everything requested behaves as pictured.
decisions.note: Conforming implemented duplicate-handling decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports tags; Round 5 client observes saved links with “my tags.”
decisions.note: Conforming implemented tag-assignment decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports advanced search; Round 5 client successfully combines “an exact phrase … and required a tag at the same time.”
decisions.note: Conforming implementation-review decision for tag, conjunction, and exact-phrase search.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports read-later; Round 5 client says the unread-only view works and read items remain in the collection.
decisions.note: Conforming implemented read-later workflow.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports formatted notes; Round 5 client observes “my formatted note kept separate from the page's own description.”
decisions.note: Conforming implemented formatted-note decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports “bulk actions”; Round 5 client states everything requested made it in and accepts the app.
decisions.note: Conforming implementation presentation for multi-selection bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports “archiving/restoration”; Round 5 client verifies archived links stay out of the main list and accepts the behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming implemented archive and restoration decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports “confirmed permanent deletion”; Round 5 client verifies confirmation before permanent delete.
decisions.note: Conforming implemented permanent-delete decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker: “Import/export remains documented for a future release.” Round 5 client: “import and export are on the books for later as we agreed — I don't need them today.”
decisions.note: At implementation review, the client explicitly acknowledges and accepts that import remains deferred.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker: “Import/export remains documented for a future release.” Round 5 client: “import and export are on the books for later as we agreed — I don't need them today.”
decisions.note: At implementation review, the client explicitly acknowledges and accepts that export remains deferred.
